question: What is the minimum attendance required to appear for the end-semester examination?
answer: You must have a minimum of 75 per cent attendance in each course, computed separately for the theory and practical components, in order to be eligible to appear for the end-semester examination in that course. Attendance is computed from the first day of instruction of the semester to the last instructional day, and includes all lectures, tutorials and practical sessions scheduled for the course.

question: How are marks split between internal assessment and the end-semester exam for a theory course?
answer: For a theory course, evaluation is out of 100 marks: 40 marks are for continuous internal assessment and 60 marks are for the end-semester examination, which is conducted by the Controller of Examinations. Internal assessment of 40 marks comprises two mid-term tests of 15 marks each (in the sixth and twelfth weeks) plus 10 marks for assignments, quizzes or tutorials.

question: What is the minimum I need to score to pass a course?
answer: To pass a course, you must score at least 30% in the end-semester examination and at least 40% of the total marks (internal assessment plus end-semester examination) combined. If either requirement is not met, you will be awarded an 'F' grade in that course. Note that meeting these marks is separate from eligibility requirements such as the 75% attendance rule.

question: What letter grade do I get for 85 marks?
answer: For 85 marks out of 100, you will receive the letter grade A+ (Excellent) with 9 grade points, since marks in the range 80 to 89 fall in that band per the grading table.

question: How many days do I have to apply for re-evaluation after results are declared?
answer: You must apply to the Controller of Examinations for re-evaluation of the answer script within ten working days of the declaration of results, on payment of the prescribed fee per course. No application shall be entertained after this period.

question: What happens if I miss an end-semester exam because I was ill?
answer: If you miss an end-semester exam because of illness, you must submit a medical certificate issued by a registered medical practitioner and countersigned by the Institute Medical Officer to the Controller of Examinations within five working days of the date of the examination. On acceptance of the certificate, you will be permitted to appear for the course in the next supplementary examination, and that appearance will be treated as your first attempt and you will be exempt from the supplementary examination fee.

question: What is the penalty if I am caught with a mobile phone in the exam hall?
answer: If you are caught with a mobile phone in the exam hall, it is treated as a first offence of using unfair means. Your examination in that course will be cancelled and you will be awarded the grade F in that course, even if the phone was switched off. Note that mobile phones are prohibited in the examination hall and possession (whether or not used) is treated as use of unfair means, so please leave your phone outside.

question: What time do the hostel gates close at night?
answer: The hostel gates close at 10:30 p.m. every day, according to the Hostel Handbook. Residents returning after the gates close must sign the late-entry register maintained by security and state the reason for the delay.

question: Can I use an induction cooktop in my hostel room?
answer: No, you cannot use an induction cooktop in your hostel room. The Hostel Handbook explicitly prohibits the use of induction cooktops (along with electric heaters, immersion rods, electric kettles, irons and any appliance rated above 500 watts) in hostel rooms, and such appliances will be confiscated with a fine of Rs. 1,000 per occurrence.

question: How much is the late fee if I pay my semester fees after the due date?
answer: If you pay your semester fees after the due date, a late fee of Rs. 100 per day is charged up to and including the last date shown in the schedule, with the late fee capped at Rs. 1,500 for any single payment. No payment is accepted after the last date, except in narrow circumstances where the Registrar permits payment due to documented delay in an education loan or scholarship disbursement.

question: What is the last date to pay the odd semester tuition fee?
answer: The last date to pay the odd semester tuition fee (along with the examination and development fee) is 31 July 2026. Payments after this date are not accepted, and a late fee applies up to this last date.

question: Who is eligible for the merit-cum-means scholarship?
answer: You are eligible for the Merit-cum-Means Scholarship if your annual family income from all sources does not exceed Rs. 3,00,000 and you have a CGPA of not less than 7.0 at the end of the preceding academic year (or, for first-year students, not less than 80 per cent marks in the qualifying examination). You must also submit an income certificate issued by a Tehsildar or an officer of equivalent rank that is not older than six months.

question: Do I get leave if there is a death in my family?
answer: Yes, you are entitled to bereavement leave of up to seven days, counted as attendance, if a parent, sibling, grandparent or spouse passes away. You must inform the HoD by e-mail or through the student portal before or during the leave, and submit a written application on your return.

question: Will I get my hall ticket if I have not paid my tuition fees?
answer: No, you will not be issued a hall ticket if you have outstanding tuition fee dues. The hall ticket will be released only within one working day after you clear the dues, provided the examination has not yet commenced. Note that if you do not pay by the last date at all, you may be treated as not registered for the semester unless the Registrar permits a late payment on specific grounds (documented delay in an education loan or scholarship).

question: How long can a break of study be?
answer: A break of study may be permitted for one semester or one academic year. AR §10.1 specifies that it is granted only on medical grounds (certified by the Institute Medical Officer and approved by the Dean) and shall not be granted more than once during the programme. Note also that under AR §10.3, the break period counts towards the seven-year maximum duration of the B.Tech. programme.

question: What is the maximum time allowed to complete the B.Tech programme?
answer: A student must complete all requirements of the B.Tech. programme within a maximum period of seven academic years from the date of first admission, failing which the student's name shall be removed from the rolls of the Institute.

question: Can I get a mess rebate if I go home for two weeks?
answer: Yes, you are entitled to a mess rebate for a two-week absence, since HH §4.3 provides that a resident absent from the hostel for a continuous period of seven days or more is entitled to a rebate of mess charges, provided the absence is recorded in the leave register in advance and the rebate form is submitted within seven days of return.

question: How much medical insurance cover do students have?
answer: Every student is covered under the group medical insurance scheme of the Institute for hospitalisation expenses of up to Rs. 1,00,000 per year. The premium is included in the development fee, and claims must be made through the Institute Medical Officer within thirty days of discharge from the hospital.

question: My attendance is 58% because I was hospitalised for three weeks. Can the shortage be condoned?
answer: The two condonation clauses give incompatible minimum-attendance thresholds for medical-grounds condonation. AR §4.3 says shortage can be condoned only if attendance is not less than 65%, and explicitly states that shortage below 65% 'shall not be condoned under any circumstances.' LM §2.2, on the other hand, allows the Dean to condone shortfall on medical grounds where attendance is 'not less than 55 per cent.' With 58% attendance, AR §4.3 forbids condonation while LM §2.2 permits it.

question: What is the lowest attendance percentage that can still be condoned on medical grounds?
answer:
The rulebook gives two different minimum-attendance thresholds for condonation on medical grounds, and they are incompatible.

1. LM §2.2 says: 'provided that the student's overall attendance in the course is not less than 55 per cent.'
2. AR §4.3 says: 'provided that the student's attendance in the course concerned is not less than 65 per cent' and 'A shortage of attendance below 65 per cent shall not be condoned under any circumstances.'

These two clauses disagree on the very question asked (the lowest condonable percentage), so no single answer can be given from the rulebook as it stands.

question: If I withdraw my admission before classes begin, how much of my tuition fee will be refunded?
answer: Two clauses give incompatible answers for a withdrawal before classes begin. [SF §6.2] says the tuition fee is refunded 'after the deduction of a processing charge of ten per cent of the tuition fee' (i.e., 90% refunded). [FS §4.1] says that withdrawal 'Before the commencement of classes' results in a refund of '100 per cent' of the tuition fee. Both passages address the same situation but specify different refund amounts, so the rulebook is in conflict.

question: What CGPA do I need to maintain to keep my merit scholarship?
answer: The passages give incompatible CGPA thresholds for continuing the Merit Scholarship. AR §11.2 requires a CGPA of not less than 7.5 at the end of each semester, while SF §3.1 requires a CGPA of not less than 8.0 at the end of each semester. These two clauses directly disagree on the same question, so you should clarify which policy applies to your case.

question: What happens if I miss the end-semester exam because of a family wedding?
answer: The rulebook does not address what happens if a student misses an end-semester exam because of a family wedding. The closest provision covers absence due to medical grounds only.

question: Can I get a re-test if I missed a mid-term test for a job interview?
answer: The rulebook does not address this situation. The closest clause covers a related case: The rulebook addresses missed mid-term tests only on medical grounds: if you submit a medical certificate to the HoD within five working days, you are entitled to a re-test within two weeks of rejoining classes. Missing a mid-term test for a job interview is not a covered ground for a re-test under that clause. However, under LM §3.3, if your interview is arranged through the Institute's Training and Placement Cell and you produce the call letter countersigned by the Placement Officer, you shall be marked present for its duration — so you may not need a re-test at all in that situation.

question: Can I change my branch after the first year?
answer: The rulebook does not address whether a student can change their branch after the first year. The closest passage, AR §3.4, only covers adding or dropping individual courses within the first two weeks of a semester, not changing branch.

question: Is there a dress code for laboratory sessions?
answer: The rulebook does not address a dress code for laboratory sessions. The closest related passage, EE §8.2, only covers the requirement that a completed and instructor-certified laboratory record must be submitted to be admitted to the end-semester practical examination.

question: Can a day scholar eat in the hostel mess by paying per meal?
answer: The rulebook does not address whether a day scholar can eat in the hostel mess on a per-meal payment basis. The closest provision simply states that every resident must be a compulsory member of the hostel mess, with mess charges paid in advance for the semester along with the hostel fee.

question: Are pets allowed in the hostel?
answer: The Hostel Handbook does not address whether pets are allowed in the hostel. The closest related passage is HH §5.4, which lists specific prohibited activities and items within the hostel.

question: What is the fee for a duplicate identity card?
answer: The rulebook does not address the fee for a duplicate identity card. The closest passage mentions the Institute identity card only as an item students must carry into the examination hall.

question: Can I get academic credit for a summer internship?
answer: The rulebook does not address whether a summer internship can count toward academic credit for the B.Tech. degree. The closest related passages describe general credit rules for courses (AR §2.2) and credit-load limits during a semester (AR §3.3).

question: Is there a scholarship for students from the EWS category?
answer: The rulebook does not address scholarships specifically for students from the EWS (Economically Weaker Section) category. The closest passage it does cover is the Merit-cum-Means Scholarship, which is awarded based on annual family income not exceeding Rs. 3,00,000 along with academic performance criteria.

question: Are grace marks given if I fail a course by one or two marks?
answer: The rulebook does not address grace marks given to a student who fails a course by one or two marks. The closest passage is AR §5.4, which sets the passing requirement of 30 per cent in the end-semester examination and 40 per cent of total marks taken together, and says that failure to meet either requirement results in an 'F' grade.

question: Can I write my answers in Hindi instead of English in the end-semester exam?
answer: The rulebook does not address whether answers may be written in Hindi instead of English in the end-semester examination. The closest passage covers the passing requirement in a course, including a separate minimum in the end-semester examination.

question: What happens if there is a printing error in the question paper?
answer: The rulebook does not address what happens if there is a printing error in the question paper. The closest passage, EE §6.2, only covers the correction of clerical errors in results within sixty days of declaration by the Controller of Examinations.

question: How do I get a duplicate degree certificate if I lose the original?
answer: The rulebook does not address the procedure for obtaining a duplicate degree certificate if the original is lost. The closest passage covers a related but different situation: it states that the original degree certificate, consolidated grade card and transfer certificate are issued only after the student obtains a no-dues certificate from the Library, Hostel Office, Department and Finance Office.

question: How many books can I borrow from the library at a time?
answer: The rulebook does not address the number of books a student may borrow from the library at a time. The closest passage is AR §12.3, which only states that the Library must issue a no-dues certificate before certain documents are released, but says nothing about borrowing limits or quotas.

question: What is the procedure to transfer to another university mid-course?
answer: The rulebook does not address the procedure for transferring to another university mid-course. The closest passage is about the no-dues certificate required before the transfer certificate is issued.

question: Can I keep a two-wheeler in the hostel parking?
answer: The rulebook does not address whether a resident may keep a two-wheeler in the hostel parking. The closest passage covers prohibited items and activities in the hostel, listing electrical appliances and other prohibitions such as gambling and keeping overnight guests, but it does not mention vehicles or parking.

question: Is there a fee concession if my sibling also studies at the institute?
answer: The rulebook does not address a fee concession on the basis of a sibling studying at the Institute. The closest passage covers a concession for children of permanent Institute staff, not siblings of current students.

question: How do I get a bonafide student certificate for my bank loan?
answer: The rulebook does not address how to obtain a bonafide student certificate for a bank loan or for any other purpose. The closest passage describes that a no-dues certificate from the Library, Hostel Office, Department and Finance Office is required before certain documents like the degree certificate, consolidated grade card and transfer certificate are issued.

question: What is the minimum CGPA to be eligible for campus placements?
answer: The rulebook does not address the minimum CGPA required for eligibility for campus placements. The closest related passage is AR §3.3, which sets a CGPA threshold of 8.5 only for the purpose of permitting an increased credit load with the Dean's approval.

question: Can I re-appear in a course I have already passed to improve my grade?
answer: The rulebook does not address whether a student may re-appear in a course they have already passed in order to improve their grade. The closest passage, AR §9.1, only allows a student who is not satisfied with their marks to apply for re-evaluation of the answer script, not to re-appear in the examination.

question: What happens if I fall ill in the middle of writing an exam?
answer: The rulebook does not address this situation. The closest clause covers a related case: If you fall ill during an exam, the rulebook does not directly address what happens while you are writing it. However, if you miss a mid-term test because of illness, you may take a re-test within two weeks of rejoining classes, provided you submit a medical certificate to the HoD within five working days of the test (EE §3.3). You should also inform the hostel supervisor or Warden immediately if you fall ill (HH §8.1).

question: How do I get my name corrected on the grade card?
answer: The rulebook does not address the procedure for getting a name corrected on the grade card. The closest passage, AR §6.3, only describes what a grade card contains (courses, credits, grades, SGPA, CGPA) and when it is issued.

question: Can I audit a course without earning credits?
answer: The rulebook does not address whether a student may audit a course without earning credits. The closest passage, AR §3.3, only sets the minimum and maximum credit load a student may register for in a semester and does not mention auditing or non-credit enrolment.

question: Is there a discount if I pay the whole year's tuition fee in advance?
answer: The rulebook does not address a discount for paying the whole year's tuition fee in advance. The closest provision, FS §2.2, only describes how tuition fees may be split into two instalments per semester and when late fees apply.

question: What is the punishment for plagiarism in a project report?
answer: The rulebook does not address the specific punishment for plagiarism in a project report. The closest passage covers the general scheme of project evaluation and submission requirements but does not mention plagiarism.
